digest.note: The on-disk hash is the check that matters: a runtime that mis-stored a blob would still report the digest it intended to store.

generation.prompt: In exactly two sentences, explain what a checksum is and why verifying one matters before installing software.
generation.reply: A checksum is a unique numerical value generated by a cryptographic algorithm that represents the contents of a file. Verifying a checksum before installing software ensures the file has not been altered or corrupted, helping to confirm its authenticity and integrity.
generation.method: measuredTokensPerSecond = eval_count / (eval_duration / 1e9), from the runtime's own instrumentation of the generation loop. wallClockTokensPerSecond divides by total HTTP round-trip time and is necessarily lower; both are recorded so the gap is visible rather than hidden.

tiersNotAttempted.why: Requires a 17.28 GiB download. Its weights alone exceed this host's 15.65 GiB of total RAM, so a hard failure is expected — and per the B3 brief that failure, with its real resource figures, IS the deliverable. It has not been run, so nothing is claimed about it either way.
tiersNotAttempted.whatWouldProveIt: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/model-tier-benchmark.mts --write --tiers qwen3:30b-a3b --out release/OCADE_B3_HEAVY_TIER_EVIDENCE.json — the failure branch records exact error, elapsed time, free RAM at the moment of failure, resident models, and the weightsExceedTotalRam flag.

measurementVariance.finding: Both runs are far below the 8B tier (5.7-6.8 tok/s) on the same machine. 8.64 GiB of weights against ~6 GiB free means Windows pages during generation, so 14B does not fail — it degrades, which is worse for a user because nothing announces it.
